project.name: LoopFlow
project.purpose: A browser-first, temporary room for sharing text messages and files between two devices.

technology.frontend: Static HTML, CSS, and native browser JavaScript modules; no bundler or build step.
technology.cloud_backend: Firebase Authentication (anonymous), Cloud Firestore, and Firebase Storage.
technology.local_backend: Dependency-free Node.js HTTP server using only built-in Node modules.

primary_entry_points.local_server: lan-server.js, normally started with node lan-server.js

runtime_modes.selection_rule: When a user creates or joins a room, app.js first checks whether the local companion service is available. It uses LAN mode when available; otherwise it uses Firebase mode.

lan.when_used: The companion service is reachable, or the room URL has mode=lan.
lan.server: lan-server.js listens on port 3847 and binds to 0.0.0.0.
lan.transport: REST-like JSON endpoints for mutations and Server-Sent Events for realtime room updates.
lan.persistence: None. Rooms, messages, and files live only in the Node process memory.
lan.lifecycle: The server deletes expired rooms every minute. Restarting the server discards all rooms immediately.
lan.network: The QR link uses the server's detected local IP, so a second device must be able to reach the PC over the same Wi-Fi network or hotspot.

firebase.when_used: The local companion service is unavailable and Firebase configuration is present.
firebase.authentication: Every browser signs in anonymously through ensureAnonymousUser().
firebase.transport: Firestore onSnapshot listeners receive room, message, and file updates in realtime.
firebase.persistence: Room metadata, messages, and file metadata live in Firestore; larger cloud-file bytes live in Firebase Storage.
firebase.fallback_behavior: If Firebase configuration or a Firebase operation is unavailable, parts of the UI retain a demo-friendly local rendering path, but this does not create a shared remote room.

room_code.format: Six random decimal digits, generated by makeRoomCode().
room_code.note: It is a convenience identifier, not a cryptographic access-control secret.

creation: app.js invokes createLocalRoom() when the companion service is reachable; otherwise it calls createRoom(code).
A Firebase room document includes roomId, createdAt, expiresAt, activeUsers, devices, ownerDeviceId, ownerId, and status.
Room lifetime is 30 minutes from creation.
join: A user enters the six-digit code or opens a QR URL.
Firebase joinRoom() validates that the room exists, is active, and has not expired.
Firebase rooms allow a maximum of two distinct device IDs. Device IDs are stored in the browser's localStorage.
LAN join requests mark the room as having up to two active users.
host_and_leave: The creator is treated as host. Leaving as host deletes/closes the room for everyone.
A non-host leaving Firebase mode removes its device ID from the room presence list.
The room page watches room state; a deleted or missing room causes joined non-host devices to leave the stale workspace.

messages.firebase: Messages are documents at rooms/{roomId}/messages, ordered by createdAt. app.js rerenders the message panel on each snapshot.
messages.lan: Messages are in the in-memory room.messages array. Every change broadcasts the whole room snapshot via the room SSE event.
messages.text_limits: LAN server limits text message content to 10,000 characters.

files.firebase: File metadata is stored at rooms/{roomId}/files, ordered by uploadedAt descending. app.js rerenders the Shared Files panel on each snapshot.
files.lan: Each file's data URL and metadata are stored in the in-memory room.files array and sent in room snapshots.
files.message_relation: Uploading a file writes both a file record and a type=file chat message in Firebase. LAN mode likewise adds the file to both room.files and room.messages.

presence.firebase: watchRoom() listens to the parent room document and updates the device count, status, host state, and countdown.
presence.lan: The room SSE snapshot contains activeUsers and expiresAt.

file_upload_pipeline.limit: validateFile() rejects files larger than 50 MiB.

firebase_strategy.condition: File size is at most 300 KiB.
firebase_strategy.action: Read the file as a base64 data URL and store that URL directly in Firestore file and message data.
firebase_strategy.reason: This stays safely below Firestore's 1 MiB document limit.

firebase_strategy.condition: File size exceeds 300 KiB and Firebase Storage makes progress.
firebase_strategy.action: Upload to Firebase Storage at rooms/{roomId}/{timestamp}_{sanitizedFileName}, retrieve its download URL, then store that URL as fileURL.

firebase_strategy.condition: Firebase Storage is unavailable, blocked by CORS, fails, or makes no progress for 3.5 seconds.
firebase_strategy.action: Split the file into 250 KiB binary chunks. Convert each chunk to a data URL and store each one at rooms/{roomId}/files/{fileId}/chunks. File metadata receives fileURL in the form chunked:{fileId}:{chunkCount}.
firebase_strategy.reason: It preserves peer transfer even when Storage cannot be used, at the cost of more Firestore documents and bandwidth.

file_upload_pipeline.lan_strategy: Read every upload as a data URL and POST it with metadata to the local server. The server keeps it in memory only.
file_upload_pipeline.single_file_download: Clicking a shared-file card intercepts navigation. app.js reconstructs chunked files from ordered Firestore chunks, converts data URLs to Blobs, or fetches cloud URLs, then triggers a browser download.

download_all_zip.ui: The Shared Files panel in chat.html contains #download-all-files-btn. It remains disabled until at least one file is present.
download_all_zip.source_of_truth: renderFiles(files) updates the in-memory currentSharedFiles list whenever the file snapshot changes.
flow: The click handler snapshots currentSharedFiles so the selected archive is stable even if a file is shared during preparation.
getFileBlob() retrieves each source: it reconstructs chunked files, converts data URLs, or fetches Firebase Storage URLs.
Duplicate and Windows-invalid names are normalized by uniqueZipName().
createZipBlob() writes a standards-compatible, uncompressed ZIP archive in the browser using local file headers, central-directory records, UTF-8 filenames, and CRC-32 checksums.
The browser downloads loopflow-room-{roomCode}.zip and revokes its temporary object URL after 10 seconds.
important_limits: The archive is built in browser memory, so very large combined downloads can exhaust device memory.
The ZIP writer is standard ZIP rather than ZIP64; extremely large archives beyond classic ZIP limits are not supported.
Cloud URLs must permit browser fetches. Existing single-file behavior falls back to opening a cloud URL when fetch fails; a ZIP cannot safely include a file that cannot be fetched.

ui_and_security_notes.rendering: app.js uses escapeHtml() before inserting file names, sender names, and message content into generated HTML. Text rendering also detects links and code-like content for richer display.
ui_and_security_notes.file_previews: Images that are not chunked can appear as lazy-loaded image previews. Other files show a short extension chip.
ui_and_security_notes.room_privacy: Rooms are temporary but are not end-to-end encrypted. Firebase security depends on the deployed Firestore and Storage rules. LAN data is accessible to devices that can access the local server and know a room code.
ui_and_security_notes.room_expiry: Countdown UI is client-side for display. Firebase expiry validation happens when joining; LAN expiry is enforced by the local server when accessing a room.

source_map.app.js: Main controller: landing actions, room page state, Firebase and LAN subscriptions, message rendering, upload UI, downloads, ZIP creation, timers, QR code, theming, and leave actions.
source_map.chat.html: Dedicated room workspace markup, including Shared Files and the Download all button.
source_map.styles.css: All visual styles, including the shared-file cards and Download all control.
source_map.room.js: Firebase room lifecycle and Firestore room presence helpers.
source_map.storage.js: Firebase file upload implementation and chunked-upload fallback.
source_map.firebase.js: Firebase SDK imports, configuration, initialized services, and anonymous-auth helper.
source_map.lan.js: Browser client for the local companion service.
source_map.lan-server.js: Local HTTP/SSE companion server, room memory store, expiration cleanup, and static-file serving.
source_map.utils.js: Shared file-type, byte-formatting, data-URL, and message-formatting helpers.
source_map.firestore.rules: Firestore access policy intended for deployment.
source_map.storage.rules: Firebase Storage access policy intended for deployment.
source_map.cors.json: Firebase Storage CORS configuration for deployed and local browser origins.
source_map.vercel.json: Vercel clean URL rewrite from /chat to chat.html.

local_run.address: http://localhost:3847 on the PC; use the QR code or detected LAN address for another device.
local_run.current_project_note: The local service is suitable for temporary same-network transfer and has no database or durable storage.

future_change_guidance: Keep LAN and Firebase behavior aligned when adding a new message or file capability.
Do not assume all fileURL values are HTTP URLs. They may be data URLs or chunked:{fileId}:{chunkCount} references.
When changing file storage, preserve the relationship between files collection records and type=file message records.
Retain the 50 MiB browser-side upload validation unless server and memory limits are updated coherently.
Test both LAN and Firebase paths, especially room creation, joining, file upload, single-file download, and ZIP download.
